maria: Hey team — seeing intermittent 500s + high tail latency (~p95-p99 spikes) when calling /v1/generate from our product. Using python SDK v0.9.2. One sample request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. Happened twice in last hour, app-side timeout after 12s.

kevin: Sorry you're hitting this, thanks for the request-id. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl + small Python/JS/Go) that we can run locally? Also if you can share the full x-request-id and any server-side log lines that'd help.

maria: quick curl I used (sanitized):
```
curl -i "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"hello","max_tokens":64}'
```
I can run snippets if you need them.

kevin: Thanks. Can you run this instrumented curl so we capture timing + headers?
```
export KEY="$REDWOOD_KEY"
time curl -w '\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\nTIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}\n' -sS -D headers.out "-H Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"hello","max_tokens":64}'
```
Upload headers.out and paste the printed timing. That helps us know whether the backend or network is the issue.

samir: adding tiny SDK repros you can run. Python minimal (requests):
```
# python repro.py
import os, requests, time
KEY = os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY')
url = 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate'
payload = {"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"hello","max_tokens":64}
start = time.time()
r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {KEY}'}, timeout=20)
print('status', r.status_code, 'elapsed', time.time()-start)
print(r.headers.get('x-request-id'))
print(r.text[:1000])
```
Node (fetch):
```
// node repro.js
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
const url = 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate'
const KEY = process.env.REDWOOD_KEY
;(async ()=>{
  const start = Date.now()
  const r = await fetch(url, {method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-alpha-1', input:'hello', max_tokens:64}), headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json', 'Authorization':`Bearer ${KEY}`}, timeout:20000})
  console.log('status', r.status, 'elapsed', Date.now()-start)
  console.log('x-request-id', r.headers.get('x-request-id'))
  console.log(await r.text())
})()
```
Go (net/http):
```
// go run repro.go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
  "time"
)
func main(){
  key := os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY")
  body := bytes.NewBufferString(`{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"hello","max_tokens":64}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate", body)
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+key)
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  client := &http.Client{Timeout: 20 * time.Second}
  start := time.Now()
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  fmt.Println("err", err)
  fmt.Println("status", resp.StatusCode, "elapsed", time.Since(start))
  fmt.Println("x-request-id", resp.Header.Get("x-request-id"))
}
```

devx-bot: Quick checklist: (1) run instrumented curl above, (2) run one SDK sample and paste x-request-id + headers.out, (3) include the full server log lines around the request-id and any GRPC gateway errors, (4) if possible run with REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 to emit trace ids.

maria: ran the python script twice, got one 500 and one 200. 500 returned headers: x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d, x-trace-id: trace-9f8e7d. time reported TIME_TOTAL: 1.21 for the 200 and 12.03 for the 500. Attached the headers.out content in thread.

kevin: Perfect, thank you. Can you also collect a lightweight debug bundle so we can correlate logs on our side? Run: 
```
REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 python repro.py > repro.log 2>&1; gzip -c repro.log > repro.log.gz
# then DM to @kevin with repro.log.gz OR upload to the secure upload link I'll DM you
```
When you DM, include the req id(s): req_0a1b2c3d and trace-9f8e7d. We'll pull server traces and check routing/batching behavior.

samir: FYI — when you see 12s and then a 500, that often indicates an internal timeout fallback path (runtime returned 500 after kernel/quant queueing). We'll check if the requests hit a degraded pool or fell back to a slower model variant.
